lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality, personal details conventionally left off.
items.because: They do not help assess the candidate’s work or qualifications and can draw attention away from relevant experience.

items.says: The 3:1 body-text contrast figure does not establish WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, and the claim does not say what was assessed or how it was verified.
items.because: Normal-sized text generally requires 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is sufficient only for large text.

items.says: The opening participial phrase does not agree with the past-tense main verb, and the result is buried after a long methods list.
items.because: The opening makes it unclear who or what cut the calls, while the list delays the outcome.

items.says: The 23% reduction has no stated comparison period or baseline.
The reader cannot tell whether the training or the shared script template doubled the number of tests.
Prototype testing with 24 customers does not establish that the shipped design caused the increase in completed sign-ups.
items.because: Prototype testing assesses usability, not the effect on real-world sign-ups; the line gives no production outcome evidence or suitable comparison.

items.says: The measurable sign-up outcome appears after the research details instead of leading the line.
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the outcome only after the prototype-testing details.

items.says: The average 0–10 recommendation rating is mislabeled as Net Promoter Score.
items.because: Standard NPS is the percentage of promoters minus the percentage of detractors, not the average rating.

items.says: The metric definition is longer than the bullet needs.
items.because: The rating-scale explanation and response count take space without making the outcome easier to scan.

items.says: The reduction in missed appointments is buried after the interview and findings clauses.
items.because: Putting the quantified reduction first would make the result easier to scan.

items.says: The two missed-appointment rates have no stated comparison periods.
“Writes” uses present tense for a role that ended in February 2022.
items.because: The tense conflicts with the entry’s dates and may make the responsibility seem current or the bullet outdated.

items.says: The 30% reduction in support calls has no stated comparison periods.
The redesign description does not say what specifically changed for screen-reader or low-vision riders.
items.because: A reader can tell who the map was intended to serve, but not what the redesign delivered for them.

items.says: The reduction from 90 to 60 seconds is 33%, not a 50% improvement.
items.because: The time fell by 30 seconds out of 90; 50% applies to the inverse-time rate, not the stated reduction in time.

items.says: The transit-map outcome is not the opening line of the project entry.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the entry’s clearest outcome because it follows the project description.

items.says: The method phrase repeats the method named in the next bullet.
The increase from 65% to 85% is 20 percentage points, not 20%.
items.because: Relative to the original 65%, the increase is about 31%.

items.says: The method phrase repeats the method named in the preceding bullet.
The redesign description does not say what the booking-flow change was.
items.because: The results show value, but not what design decision or skill contributed to them.

items.says: The line does not say whether users completed bookings more successfully after the six issues were fixed.
items.because: The issue count shows what was addressed, but not whether the changes improved booking completion in practice.

items.says: “interveiws” is misspelled in the Methods skills line.
items.because: The visible typo can distract a reader from the candidate’s qualifications.
